stem: That same insurance company also runs a customer-facing application backed by Amazon S3 that needs every new object also available for low-latency reads in a second Region within 15 minutes of being written, in addition to the point-in-time recovery already provided by AWS Backup. Which TWO features close this gap? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: S3 Batch Replication run once against the bucket's existing objects
Relying on AWS Backup's existing cross-Region copy job on its own
Cross-Region Replication (CRR) configured on the bucket
S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) enabled on the replication rule
S3 Versioning enabled only on the destination bucket

rationale: Cross-Region Replication asynchronously copies new and updated objects to a second Region going forward, which is the ongoing live copy this scenario needs, and S3 Replication Time Control adds the service-level agreement to replicate 99.99% of new objects within 15 minutes, meeting the stated time bound. S3 Batch Replication replicates objects that already existed before replication was configured; it does not keep replicating new writes going forward on its own. AWS Backup's cross-Region copy job protects point-in-time recovery points on a backup schedule, not a near-real-time copy of every new object as it is written. Enabling versioning only on the destination bucket protects against accidental overwrite there, but it does not replicate anything from the source bucket or provide any replication time guarantee.
